skill.name: dx-optimizer
skill.description: Improves developer experience by reducing setup friction, automating repeatable workflows, and strengthening project tooling, documentation, and feedback loops.
skill.summary: Optimize setup, tooling, scripts, documentation, and feedback loops for faster development workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Development teams lose time to slow setup, unclear scripts, and inconsistent tooling. This skill audits workflows and recommends practical improvements for onboarding, automation, documentation, and feedback loops.
actual_capabilities: Profile current developer workflows and identify pain points.
Recommend faster setup paths for new contributors.
Suggest useful scripts, aliases, commands, and task runners.
Improve README, setup, and troubleshooting documentation.
Define measurable success metrics for DX changes.
limitations: Requires project context before recommending tools or scripts.
May need maintainer validation before changing build, test, or hook behavior.
Does not provide runtime benchmarks unless measurements are supplied or collected.
Does not replace project-specific architectural review.

use_cases.title: New Project Onboarding
use_cases.description: A tech lead uses the skill to shorten clone-to-run setup and document required commands.

use_cases.title: Workflow Automation
use_cases.description: A developer uses the skill to convert repeated manual steps into scripts, aliases, or task runner commands.

use_cases.title: Tooling Health Review
use_cases.description: A platform engineer uses the skill to review IDE settings, git hooks, and test feedback loops.

prompt_templates.title: Find Setup Friction
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project from a new contributor viewpoint. Identify setup steps, unclear commands, and documentation gaps that slow onboarding.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Daily Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze our build, test, lint, and local run workflows. Recommend script names, aliases, and task runner changes that reduce repetitive work.

prompt_templates.title: Design a DX Improvement Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased DX improvement plan for this repository. Include priorities, expected impact, verification steps, and rollback considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Feedback Loops
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate our hot reload, test execution, git hooks, and CI handoff. Propose measurable changes that reduce waiting time and confusion.

output_examples.input: A repository has a long README, several manual setup steps, and unclear local run commands.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a prioritized setup audit with faster onboarding steps, clearer command naming, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: A team repeats manual lint, test, and branch checks before every pull request.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes consolidated commands, git hook guidance, and review steps that reduce repeated manual work.

output_examples.input: A project has slow tests and inconsistent IDE settings across contributors.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies feedback loop bottlenecks and suggests shared settings, faster checks, and measurable success metrics.

best_practices: Start with the current developer journey before adding tools.
Measure setup time, command count, and feedback loop speed before and after changes.
Keep automation discoverable through README updates and command help text.
anti_patterns: Adding scripts without explaining when to use them.
Automating risky workflow steps without review or rollback guidance.
Treating developer complaints as tooling problems before checking documentation and process.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It focuses on setup, tooling, automation, documentation, and feedback loops that affect daily developer work.

faq.question: Can it change repository files?
faq.answer: It can recommend or help implement changes when the user grants normal editing permission.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for new projects?
faq.answer: No. It also helps existing teams reduce repeated tasks and improve maintainability.

faq.question: What inputs help most?
faq.answer: Share the repository, current setup steps, common commands, team pain points, and any timing data.

faq.question: Can it benchmark performance?
faq.answer: It can define metrics and interpret measurements, but benchmark results require actual project runs.
